body:
`LedgerDevice::open()` currently hard-wires USB HID, so emulator and recorded-APDU tests have to duplicate the core's protocol implementation. This adds `ApduTransport: Send + Sync` and `LedgerDevice::with_transport`, allowing the same request building, chunking, answer parsing and status-word handling to run over an injected transport.

The HID exchange implementation moves unchanged behind the trait, and `open()` keeps its existing API. The trait is available without the `ledger` feature and on wasm32; the device constructor remains `ledger`-gated. The short-answer error now says "APDU response" for all transports.

Three unit tests preserve `LedgerDevice: Send + Sync`, check exact INIT/ADD/LAST bytes for a 300-byte payload plus a 200-byte proof, and verify the existing `0x6986` refusal message. No runtime, dependency or lockfile changes.

Validated on Rust 1.89/macOS arm64, with `--locked` for Cargo build/test checks and `PYO3_NO_PYTHON=1` for the binding checks:

- `cargo test -p bittensor-core --all-features --lib`: 74 passed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo test -p bittensor-core --all-features --lib signers::`: 5 passed, including the 3 added tests.
- `cargo clippy -p bittensor-core -p bittensor-core-py --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.
- `cargo check -p bittensor-core --no-default-features`, with and without `--features ledger`.
- `cargo check -p bittensor-core --no-default-features --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- `cargo check -p bittensor-core-py` and package-scoped `cargo fmt --check`.

A prior prototype of this transport change at `v477` drove the core's `ledger.rs` against Speculos 0.27.1 and the Polkadot generic app 100.0.29, then replayed the recorded exchanges. That emulator evidence is from the prototype; the current PR was validated with the Rust checks above. No physical-device run or full monorepo preflight was performed for this PR.
title: sdk: allow injecting the Ledger APDU transport
